la:noun:prudentia.html:
prūdentĭa, ae, f.
prudens
.
A foreseeing (very rare): id enim est sapientis providere: ex quo sapientia est appellata prudentia, ap. : futurorum,.—
Acquaintance with a thing, knowledge of a matter, skill in a matter: juris publici,: juris civilis,: legum,; cf. : physicorum,: cani rectoris,; .—
Esp., = juris prudentia, praef. § 2.—
Sagacity, good sense, intelligence, prudence, practical judgment, discretion: prudentia constat ex scientiā rerum bonarum et malarum et nec bonarum nec malarum,: prudentia tribus partibus constare videtur, memoriā, intellegentiā, providentiā,; cf. : prudentia, quam Graeci φρόνησιν, est rerum expetendarum fugiendarumque scientia, : prudentia cernitur in delectu bonorum et malorum,: ut medicina valetudinis, sic vivendi ars est prudentia,: civilis prudentia,statesmanship,; : ad omnes res adhibere prudentiam,; ; : rerum fato prudentia major,: velox,ready,: si ratio et prudentia curas aufert,.

la:adj:prudens.html:
prūdens, entis, adj.
contr. from providens
.
Foreseeing, foreknowing (very rare); constr. with an objective clause, or absol.: ille contra urinam spargit, prudens, hanc quoque leoni exitialem,: quos prudentis possumus dicere, id est providentis,: de futuro satis callidus satisque prudens, Ps.-Sall. ap. Cic. init.—
Transf.
Knowing, skilled, experienced, versed, practised in a thing (class.; syn.: peritus, consultus); constr. with gen. or in;poet. and post-Aug. also with inf.
With gen.: ceterarum rerum pater familias et prudens et attentus,: belli prudentes, Sall. Ep. Mith. (H. 4, 61, 16 Dietsch): rei militaris,: locorum,: animus rerum prudens,: artis,: animorum provinciae prudens,: doli prudens,: agricolationis,.—Comp.: prudentiores rerum rusticarum,; so, earum rerum,.—Sup.: adulandi gens prudentissima,.—
With in: prudens in jure civili,.—
With inf. or acc. and inf.: nec pauperum prudens anus Novemdialis dissipare pulveres,: prudens otii vitia negotio discuti,:-ob ea se peti prudens, : sciens prudensque se praegnantem non esse,.—
In partic.
Juris prudens, also prudens alone (like juris peritus), skilled or learned in the law; as subst.: jūrisprūdens, ntis, m., one learned in the law, a lawyer, jurist, jurisconsult (only post-class.), ; ; ; 40, 7, 30; .—
Like sciens, knowing, wise, discreet, prudent; usually connected with sciens: prudens animam de corpore mitto, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 216 Vahl.): quos prudens praetereo,; (cf.: imprudens praeteriisse videris,): ibis sub furcam prudens,: nequidquam deus abscidit Prudens Oceano terras,; ; : an prudens imprudensve rupisset,.—With sciens: amore ardeo: et prudens, sciens, Vivus vidensque pereo,: ut in fabulis Amphiaraus sic ego prudens et sciens ad pestem ante oculos positam sum profectus,; Cael. ap. , A, 5; —
In gen., sagacious, sensible, intelligent, clever, judicious, etc. (very freq.): vir naturā peracutus et prudens,: quis P. Octavio ingenio prudentior, jure peritior,: prudentem et, ut ita dicam, catum,: in existimando admodum prudens,; cf.: prudentissimi in disserendo,: virum ad consilia prudentem,: quo nemo prudentior,: homines amicissimi ac prudentissimi,: vir bonus et prudens,; cf. : si divitiae prudentem reddere possent,: prudentior ille consilio, hic animo magnificentior,.—With adverb. acc.: prudens alia,.—Of abstract things: prudens, temperata, fortis, justa ratio,: prudens animi sententia,: consilium, quod si non fuerit prudens, Balb. ap. , A, 1; : prudentissimum consilium,; . —
Cautious, circumspect (very rare): malebant me nimium timidum quam satis prudentem existimari,.— Hence, adv.: prūdenter, sagaciously, intelligently, discreetly, wisely, skilfully, learnedly, prudently, etc.: loqui, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 255 Vahl.): facere,; cf. : rationem excogitare,: multa ab eo prudenter disputata,: multa provisa prudenter,.—Comp., Aug. in 21; .—Sup.: defendere,: scribere,; ext. 4.

Prūsĭas, ae, and Prūsĭa, ae, m., = Προυσίας,
a king of Bithynia, who hospitably received Hannibal, but afterwards betrayed him to the Romans, ; ; ; ; ext.—Form Prusia, .—Hence,
Prūsĭăcus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Prusias, Prusiacan: orae,i. e. his kingdom,.—
Prūsĭădes, ae, m., a male descendant of (an older) Prusias, a Prusiade, applied to king Prusias himself, Varr. ap. .
